claims.claim: Residents pay wealth tax on worldwide net wealth above 72,000 UVT (COP 3.77bn, about $1.2M; 2026)

sources.name: PwC: Colombia, other taxes
sources.says: Last reviewed 21 July 2026. Equity tax is triggered by holding net wealth on 1 January "in excess of 72,000 UVT (COP 3,770,928,000 for 2026)"; marginal bands 0% to 72,000 UVT, 0.5% to 122,000, 1.0% to 239,000 and 1.5% above, the "1.5% tax rate will apply only for 2023, 2024, 2025, and 2026". "There is no inheritance or gift-specific tax, as such, in Colombia": inheritances are taxed to the heir as a capital (occasional) gain, and "The general tax rate for capital gains in Colombia is 15%".

sources.name: DIAN: Concepto 008914 de 2026
sources.says: Dated 27 May 2026. Under art. 294-3 ET the tax arises from holding patrimony on 1 January "cuyo valor sea igual o superior a setenta y dos mil (72.000) UVT"; the 40,000 UVT threshold added for 2026 by Decreto Legislativo 1474 de 2025 was suspended and then declared inexequible in Sentencia C-079 de 2026, so it cannot be used to require filing or payment for 2026.

sources.name: Accounter: ABC del impuesto al patrimonio 2025
sources.says: Dated 20 May 2025. Gross patrimony includes "bienes en el exterior (para residentes)"; rates under art. 296-3 ET: 0.5% from 72,000 to 122,000 UVT, 1.0% to 239,000 UVT, 1.5% above 239,000 UVT.

sources.name: DIAN: Concepto general 006365 (int 619) de 2023 on the wealth tax
sources.says: Dated 29 May 2023. Art. 292-3 numeral 1 makes resident individuals who are income taxpayers liable; numerals 2 and 3 make non-residents liable only on patrimony "poseído directamente en el país" or held through a permanent establishment. Residence follows art. 10 ET and is assessed on 1 January.

claims.note: PwC gives the threshold and amount but not the reach; the worldwide reach for residents rests on DIAN 6365 (non-residents liable only on patrimony in Colombia, residents without that limit) and Accounter. COP 3.77bn at the repo's fx.json rate (COP 3,240 per USD, 7 Nov 2026) is about $1.16M. localTaxes.ts (CO) agrees: 72,000 UVT, 0.5% then 1%.

claims.claim: So there is no US credit for the Colombian tax on US-sited stocks

sources.name: Cornell LII: 26 U.S. Code § 2014, credit for foreign death taxes
sources.says: Subsection (a): the estate tax is credited with foreign estate, inheritance, legacy or succession taxes "actually paid to any foreign country in respect of any property situated within such foreign country" and included in the gross estate.
